setup: Lie on your back, one knee bent
Other leg straight on the floor
Hands flat under your lower back
execution: Brace gently, as if before a cough
Lift head and shoulders just a little
faults: Don't flatten or arch your lower back
Don't tuck your chin to your chest
Don't curl up into a full crunch

notes: The lift is small on purpose: head, neck and shoulders rise as one, only slightly off the floor.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Curl-up with head supported
regressions.reason: Brace and hold without lifting the head.

progressions.name: Curl-up with elbows lifted
progressions.reason: Raising the elbows off the floor adds a little demand.

progressions.name: Longer holds or more reps
progressions.reason: Build endurance before adding anything harder.

substitutions.name: Dead bug
substitutions.reason: Back-lying trunk control with no curl.

substitutions.name: Side plank
substitutions.reason: Another of the same three-exercise set; works the sides.

substitutions.name: Bird dog
substitutions.reason: Third exercise of the same set; works the back of the trunk.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at floor level, head on the left. The bent knee is the near leg so both legs read clearly. Hands visible under the lower back.

keyPositions.label: Rest
keyPositions.describe: Lying on the back, near knee bent with the foot flat, far leg straight. Hands palm-down under the small of the back, keeping its natural curve. Head on the floor.

keyPositions.label: Hold
keyPositions.describe: Head, neck and shoulders lifted together a few centimetres off the floor; the chin is not tucked. Lower back still resting on the hands with its curve kept.

ikHints: Hands stay under the lower back
emphasise: Head and neck move as one with the shoulders
Lower back curve kept on the hands
